HR 30m (confirm you are human and initial connection - sometimes this could come after HM interview depending on how quickly the HM is trying to move and how fast HR person is able to go)

Loop day
Round 1: Met with a Principal Program Manager. Behavioral questions around customer obsession and past experiences. Really had a good conversation. Had a good feeling out of this round.

Round 2: Met with Senior PM. Behavioral questions, conflict resolution, and a hypothetical scenario on Critical customer issue and how to approach. Really connected well with interviewer. Had a pretty good feeling coming out of this round.

Round 3: Met with Principal PM Manager. Behavioral questions, Technical challenges faced in past experiences, Experience in cloud. Great connect with interviewer and he went on to mention that I would be a good fit for this role and they had couple of positions open. He also leads a team of 3PM's and looking to add one more.

Round 4: Met with Hiring Manager. Looks like She leads the Principal PM managers and PM's report to Principal PM Manager. Few Behavioral questions, Questions on resume and past experience, Complex tech challenge, Most valuable learnings. I felt like she didn't got the answers she was looking fine. I didn't felt really good coming out of this interview.

Shortly after being hired, they found out their team's hiring goals included targeting one diversity candidate as after she was hired she saw they had updated and submitted their KR for it. 

For individuals hired to meet diversity targets, it often becomes painfully apparent shortly after starting the role. Therefore, I recommend having an early transition plan in place to switch teams. Toxic teams typically do not transform overnight. It is the responsibility of management working with HR  to shift the team culture. The person being hired into that environment immediately faces negative assumptions and potential resentment from the first day simply due to inherent traits unrelated to their job performance or worse yet the perception they took away someone else’s job who was “more qualified”.  

Some individuals struggle to separate a person's race and gender from their perceived ability to do the work. Amazon is doing this too.  They haven't moved bands down yet (I don't think) but they are making lower offers and have warned RSU refreshers in the future will be lower. sharing my experience interviewing for a Program Manager role at Microsoft for their data center.

Total Interview Duration: Around 1 month. The process extended due to the July 4th holiday, causing my full interview loop to be spread across three different weeks.

Timeline:

Early June: I found the job posting on LinkedIn and reached out to the HM via LinkedIn to discuss my potential fit for the role. A few days later, I received a message from the recruiter to schedule an interview with the HM, along with a list of logistical and administrative questions to answer via email.

Mid June: I had the first phone screen with the HM. We delved deeply into the role, expectations, and the qualities the HM was looking for in a candidate + questions. 

Late June - Early July: The full interview loop consisted of 4 rounds. One round was with a cross-functional team member, and the remaining three were with program managers from the same team.

This experience was quite different from the TPM interviews I've had with other FANG companies. Unlike those, which typically involve specific subject-focused rounds, there were no system design or technical rounds in this process. However, the interviewers were interested in my knowledge of data centers deployments, focusing more on conceptual understanding rather than deep technical details. Instead of general boilerplate questions, the majority of the interviews centered around my past projects and a few behavioral questions.
